newsitem.title: USA: Sen. Daschle sees close budget amendment vote.
newsitem.headline: Sen. Daschle sees close budget amendment vote.

text.p: U.S. Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle said Tuesday he now sees a vote on the balanced budget amendment to the U.S. Constitution as "too close to call."
Last week he had said the amendment would pass if the vote were held then.

Daschle, a South Dakota Democrat, also said he understood President Clinton would meet with congressional leaders of both parties next week to discuss balancing the budget and a range of other issues.

Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott and House Speaker Newt Gingrich invited Clinton to come to Capitol Hill Wednesday. The White House replied that Clinton was interested in the bipartisan talks but would be out of town Feb.5.
"As I understand it, that will take place next week," Daschle said at his regular news conference.

On the separate issue of a constitutional amendment to require a balanced budget, the Senate is to begin Wednesday. The White House has stepped up its opposition and an effort to exempt Social Security trust funds from the balanced budget has gained momentum among House Republicans.

Daschle told reporters the opposition was picking up votes. "If the vote were held today, I don't know. I honestly don't. I know there has been movement but I don't know what the net effect of the movement is. But it is too close to call," he said.
The amendment must be approved by two thirds of the House and Senate and then has seven years to be ratified by 38 of the 50 states. It would not take effect before 2002.

The president is to present his fiscal 1998 budget Feb. 6, kicking off the start of negotiations on reaching a balanced budget by the year 2002. The White House has stated his plan will show the path to a balanced budget in five years with nearly $100 billion in tax cuts.
